note:
**Coverage.** Twenty-three pages, thirty-nine measured regions on seventeen of them, all
accounted once: twenty-six figure rows, seven table rows and six excluded regions. The
row count exceeds the exhibit count in the other direction from most papers in this run:
twenty-four printed exhibits produce thirty-three rows because three of them are pasted as
several separate boxes, and two printed exhibits (the symbol table, and Appendix 2's three
array screenshots) have to be found without a caption detector's help.

**This is a resale scan too, and it uses the same watermark.** A Chinese shop line
("精品数模资料，...淘宝店铺：闵大荒工科男的杂货铺！") prints above nine of the
region-bearing pages and the layout pass reads it as `caption_above` on every raster that
opens a page. It is never a caption. The second lie is native to this paper: the line
"Figure 4.5." at the foot of p8 is the LAST LINE OF A BODY PARAGRAPH - "the location of
the stations in the Figure 4.5." - flush left at the body margin, and the caption detector
counted it as a caption because it starts with the token. The real Figure 4.5 caption is
centred on p9. Eighteen caption strings in the text layer, seventeen captions.

**The prose is partly invisible.** All six excluded regions are prose or equations
pasted as rasters rather than artwork: p6 and p7 hold the derivation of the pixel-honeycomb
model, p11 three paragraphs plus four formulas of the service-capacity section, p12 the
logistic growth model, p14 the closing of the 4.3.1 cost factor and p15 the P/TC/AI
formulas. p7 returns no text layer at all, and its single 497x652 pt box would read as the
paper's largest figure to any regions-only census. Every one of those blocks is text the
paper expects to be read, which means a text-derived analysis of this paper undercounts
its prose by roughly a page and a half.

**The exhibit that is not a figure.** The symbol table on p4 is a 581x355 printed bitmap
of a ruled two-column table, pasted into section 3 with its title baked in - so it has
rules, a header and thirteen rows but no caption anywhere and no text in the layer. It is
recorded as a table with caption source `none`. The two control-engineering schematics
(the p5 block diagram and the 4.3.2 decision chart) and the handout's three-segment range
aid are the paper's other uncaptioned exhibits. Four exhibits, no caption, no number.

**Custody, box by box.** Figure 4.1 is SIX panels in a 3x2 paste, and the caption sits
6.2 pt under the bottom-right panel; the control diagram 265 pt above it belongs to the
previous paragraph and is not part of the figure. Figure 4.8 is three boxes across the top
of p12 under one caption - and its third panel is bit-identical to Figure 4.7, the same
embedded image object reused, so the set prints one drawing twice under two numbers.
Appendix 2's caption takes custody of three stacked array screenshots. This is the paper
where "one caption, N boxes" is the norm rather than the exception: nine of thirty-three
rows are panels.

**Wide box, wrong exhibit.** p15 is the trap of the paper. The largest ink on the page is a
497x278 pt block and the real Figure 4.11 is the 345x146 pt bar 87 pt below it with its
caption 6.1 pt under that. The same shape recurs on p14 (the wide box is the 4.3.1 formula
paste; Figure 4.10 is the pair of bar panels below) and on p11 (the wide box is the
service-capacity prose; Table 4.5 is the grid at the foot). A detector that ranks by area
picks the wrong exhibit on three consecutive pages.

**Headerless is not the norm here - the opposite is.** Five of the seven grids print a
real header row, unlike the surrounding papers in this run, and the two that do not are
the extremes: the symbol table (header baked into the bitmap) and Appendix 3 (no header,
62 entries, 31 rows, full measure). All seven are boxed except the symbol table; none has
zebra, merged cells, a diagonal header, a unit line or decimal alignment. The unit always
rides inside the value cell as the word 'million' or 'thousand'.

**Citation is dense but inert.** Twelve exhibits are named by number - the 4.1 and 4.2
stretches name two in one sentence ("shown in the Table 4.3 and the location in the Figure
4.6") - but no exhibit is ever named twice, the appendix is promised twelve pages before
it prints, and the three US maps that are meant to be read in sequence are never
cross-referenced to each other at all.

**Apparatus limits worth keeping.** The caption of Figure 4.11 prints as 'Figure 4. 11'
with a space inside the number and the prose calls it 'Figure 4.11', so the recorded
numbering follows the printed string while the citation style follows the prose. Table
4.1's Rural total is arithmetically wrong (1.20 + 0.04 prints as 1.20). Table 4.5's rows
come back from the text layer out of order, which is extraction, not layout. And Figure
5.1's caption sits 1.3 pt under its box - welded, and the tightest caption gap in the
paper.


Excluded regions, one line each.

p14r1: Prose-and-formula screenshot closing the 4.3.1 cost factor begun on p13 - the optimised urgency indicator, in a 479x109 pt grayscale raster. Body text resumes at y182, which is what separates it from Figure 4.10's box below: the caption under Figure 4.10 takes custody of that box only.
p15r1: The largest block on p15 and not the figure: 497x278 pt of pasted prose plus the P, TC and AI formulas of section 4.3.2, in grayscale, ending at body text on y378. Figure 4.11 is the SMALL box 87 pt below it, and its caption prints 6.1 pt under that small box - the single most likely mis-attribution in the paper.
rules: Thirty-nine measured regions on seventeen of twenty-three pages resolve to thirty-three exhibit rows - twenty-six figures and seven tables - for TWENTY-FOUR printed exhibits, plus six exclusions, and every region is claimed exactly once [place.doc_order].

The surplus of nine rows is pure custody, not double counting: Figure 4.1 is six separately pasted panels, Figure 4.8 three and Appendix 2 three array screenshots, so the region-to-exhibit join here has to be made box by box [place.page_order].

Placement is section-driven: the whole 4.x model block takes twenty-five of the thirty-three rows, the appendix takes five, the symbol front matter one and the handout and the technology section two [place.section_kind].

Artwork tracks the sub-model rather than the exhibit type - 4.1.1 carries the pixel-honeycomb panels, 4.1.2 the three US maps and three grids, 4.2.3 the growth curve, 4.3.1 the bar pair and 4.3.2 the range bar [place.section_path].

Rows sit high on the page: fourteen in the top third, thirteen in the middle and six at the foot, and not one exhibit takes a page - the largest covers 47.8 per cent of its page, and that is Appendix 3's listing, not a figure [place.page_zone].

Caption side is a property of the PART of the paper, and it inverts at the appendix: every numbered body figure prints its caption BELOW its artwork, while Appendix 1, Appendix 2 and Appendix 3 all print ABOVE, outside the box [caption.position].

Numbering is section-prefixed and unpunctuated - 'Figure 4.1', 'Table 4.1' with a space and no colon or full stop - and it jumps to a new counter at the last section as 'Figure 5.1' [caption.numbering].

Two exhibits carry no number at all: the symbol table, whose title is baked into its bitmap, and the three uncaptioned schematics, so a census keyed on caption labels misses three pieces of authored artwork outright [caption.words].

Every caption is a single bare noun phrase with no verb: voice is `none` on all twenty-nine quoted captions, no caption states a unit, none names a variable, none gives a condition and none draws a conclusion [caption.voice].

Captions run longer than this run's average - median ten words, longest fifteen, shortest six, with only one under seven - because every one of them carries a country or region qualifier after the noun [caption.words].
The artwork is cartographic first: eight map-or-plan-view rows, seven line rows, three bar rows, three flowcharts, three table-as-figure rasters, one composite and one scatter [geometry.family].

Not one of the twenty-six figures carries a legend, and not one needs to: the in-panel MATLAB titles on Figure 4.1 ('num-station', 'investment situation', 'Step Response'), the axis labels that name their own subject, the arrow annotations on Figure 4.11 and the place names printed inside the appendix artwork all do the key's work [geometry.legend].
No colourbar anywhere, not even on the two density maps, which read as continuous ramps with the scale explained only in prose [geometry.colorbar].
Nothing is three-dimensional: zero perspective bars, zero surface meshes, zero isometric axes across all twenty-six figures [geometry.three_d].

Panels are pasted, not laid out: nine rows are explicitly marked as panels of a sibling row, and three exhibits (Figure 4.2, Figure 4.10, Figure 5.1) hold two panels inside ONE box with independent y axes and no shared scale [geometry.panel_count].
Printed numbers are the axis furniture only - Figure 4.9's stage years and Figure 4.11's 0/0.2/0.65/1 tick row - and no figure prints a value on the data itself [geometry.printed_numbers].

Two of Figure 4.1's six panels are EMPTY: the axes, ticks and titles are drawn and no series is plotted, a defect only a crop shows and one that a region census records as two perfectly good line charts [geometry.data_labels].

Table size tracks the data and only the appendix grows tall: four or five rows everywhere in the body, fourteen in the symbol bitmap, and thirty-one physical rows in Appendix 3's county listing [table.rows].

Column count is fixed at four for every measurement grid - a stub plus destination, supercharging and total - and Appendix 3 reaches four only because it prints two rank-name pairs side by side [table.cols].

Five of the seven table rows print a real header row; the symbol table's header is baked into its raster, and Appendix 3 prints NONE - its row one starts half a point under the top rule and the rank column does the header's work [table.header_rows].

Rules split by provenance: the five body grids and Appendix 3 are completely BOXED in 0.48 pt horizontals and verticals on a 16.8 pt pitch, while the symbol table is the paper's only horizontal-only booktabs-style grid [table.rule_style].

There is no row shading in the entire paper - no zebra on any of the seven grids, and the only fill primitives outside the artwork are the page-header rule and the highlight boxes inside pasted screenshots [table.zebra].
No cell is merged anywhere, no header is diagonal, and no grid carries a split or two-tier header [table.merged_cells].

Not one grid puts a unit in its header or in a line above it: the unit rides inside every value cell as the word 'million' or 'thousand', which is why the appendix's inline urban_area / rural_area tag is a column VALUE rather than a unit [table.units_in_header].

No grid aligns on the decimal point: the values are centred as strings, so '14.62 thousand' in Table 4.4 sits three points right of the 8.44 and 6.18 above it even though all three carry two decimals [table.decimal_aligned].
Six of the seven grids stop at 83 to 88 per cent of the measure, which is a uniform 414.6 to 414.9 pt for the five body grids, and only Appendix 3 runs the full width at 459.3 pt [table.width].

No table continues across a page break, though the appendix's county listing runs to sixty-two entries and one body paragraph is carried to the next page in the middle of a sentence [table.continued].

Citation is frequent but shallow: seventeen rows carry a numbered reference in the prose and twelve distinct exhibits are ever named - eight of them in the 4.1 and 4.2 stretches where one sentence names two exhibits at once [mention.style].

Sixteen rows are never named at all: the symbol table, the three uncaptioned schematics (p5, p14 and the handout), Figures 4.2, 4.4, 4.8 and 4.10, Table 4.1, Table 4.5 and all four appendix boxes, which arrive by layout alone [mention.first_page].

A lead sentence is present for twenty-six of thirty-three rows and it always names the subject rather than the artwork: 'the result is shown below:', 'The specific steps of the model are as follows:' [mention.lead_sentence].
Only eight rows quote a reading sentence, and the densest stretch is section 4.1 where each map is followed by a sentence telling the reader what to see [mention.trail_sentence].

Three exhibits are introduced one page before they print - Figure 4.1, Figure 4.5 and Figure 4.9 - and one twelve pages before: Appendix 3 is promised on p11 in the middle of the dynamic-programming section and printed on p23 [mention.lead_pages].
Counts are one everywhere they exist: no exhibit is cited twice anywhere in the paper, not even the three maps that are meant to be read as a sequence [mention.count].

tables.note: The symbol table, and the reason this paper's exhibit count cannot be read off the caption list: it is a 581x355 px BITMAP of a ruled table pasted into the symbols section, so none of its words reach the text layer and it carries no Table number. Two columns - symbol and definition - over thirteen symbol rows, with HORIZONTAL-ONLY rules (one under the header, one under the column titles, one at the foot) and no vertical rules at all, so the style is `booktabs` even though the table is set by hand in Word. The title 'Symbols and Definitions' is baked into the raster and stands in for the caption, which is why the caption is recorded as source `none` with an empty quote: there is no citable text.
